name: Throat coat tea

lead: Throat Coat-style teas are drunk for a soothed throat and a clearer, more comfortable voice, especially around heavy voice use by singers and speakers.

They are commonly built around slippery elm, whose inner bark has long been used in folk medicine for sore throat and is sold in the US as an over-the-counter demulcent, a coating soothing agent. Use is traditional, and no clinical studies of these teas were found.

paras: People drink the tea warm before or after heavy talking or singing, as part of a wider voice-care routine alongside water and rest.
The sources reviewed did not describe adverse effects.
